executive_summary: Agents.md was evaluated directly as the object under test against the supervisory-gate failures observed across recent runs. The analysis reveals a combination of: (1) requirements already present in Agents.md but violated or circumvented by controller and model implementations (e.g. failing Step 0 gate, missing key repair, strict step ordering); and (2) material omissions and ambiguities in Agents.md itself. Agents.md lacks explicit definitions for the unevaluated supervisory gate initial template state (evaluative fields = null), lacks an explicit requirement to evaluate user-requested deliverables (like generated skills/artifacts) against every stated requirement before passing gates, omits concrete return-schema examples for supervisory states (Step 0 return, unevaluated gate, completed PASS/FAIL gates, restart on FAIL, commit checkpoints), lacks any durable Git commit checkpointing rule (requiring at least N commits for an N-step procedure), and does not explicitly forbid the model or runner from polluting verbatim user_request/U with internal orchestration strings like 'Perform exactly Step N'.

agents_md_reference.requirement: Step 0 defines start_of_turn schema requiring run_nonce, user_request, current_timestamp, return_schema_completed: false, return_schema_completed_timestamp: null, nonce. The supervisory gate mandates: 'The next execution step is permitted only when gate_result is PASS. Select FAIL otherwise. Do not begin the next execution step when this value is FAIL.'

program_reference.behavior: Runner executes Step 0 and enforces gate_result === 'PASS' before advancing, but Agents.md lacks explicit criteria detailing what constitutes a Step 0 execution failure (e.g. non-verbatim user_request, missing/mismatched run_nonce or nonce, uncompleted storage write).

requirement_evaluations.explanation: Agents.md states that gate_result must be PASS before Step 1, but its Step 0 definition (lines 121-124) only provides an abstract description without an explicit checklist of disqualifying execution discrepancies. Without explicit gate criteria in Step 0 granular mirror instructions, models evaluate imperfect returns as PASS.
requirement_evaluations.required_change: In Agents.md Step 0 Supervisory Gate, add explicit granular verification rules: if run_nonce does not match bootstrap run_nonce, if user_request does not match verbatim user utterance, if nonce is absent or invalid, or if return_schema_completed is not false, granular evaluation must be FAIL and gate_result must be FAIL.

agents_md_reference.requirement: Supervisory gates instruct the supervisor to mirror every returned key and replace execution values with evaluation and comment, but present the schema with placeholders like '<required supervisor evaluation...>'.

program_reference.behavior: Controller attempts to synthesize an unevaluated gate object by replacing values with null and passing it in prompt context.

requirement_evaluations.explanation: Agents.md does not specify the initial state of the supervisory gate schema. It does not state that the gate schema begins unevaluated with every evaluative field, granular terminal entry, step-level evaluation, comment, and gate_result initialized to null, nor does it forbid pre-populating evaluative fields or prompting toward a predetermined PASS/FAIL result.
requirement_evaluations.required_change: Add an explicit section to Agents.md establishing the Unevaluated Supervisory Gate Protocol: Every supervisory gate starts from an unevaluated schema template where all evaluative and comment fields (granular evaluation/comment, step_level_evaluation evaluation/comment, and gate_result) are strictly null. The supervisor semantic operation must receive this unevaluated template alongside the execution return and populate it.

agents_md_reference.requirement: Step 2 extracts stated requirements verbatim. Step 3 constructs plan P and proposed UI output. Supervisory gate requires evaluating complete step as a unit including relationships among returned entries, governing instructions, and user request.

program_reference.behavior: Supervisors routinely grant PASS to execution steps that populate required schema keys (e.g. Step_3.D.P or UI_output) even when the actual work product or deliverable omitted core components required by the user.

requirement_evaluations.explanation: Agents.md lacks an explicit imperative requiring the Step 3 and Step 4 supervisory gates to trace the actual proposed plan P, proposed deliverable content, and UI output against EVERY individual stated requirement extracted in Step 2. Because Agents.md only directs the supervisor to 'evaluate the complete step as a unit', models treat structural schema presence as substantive satisfaction.
requirement_evaluations.required_change: Add an explicit deliverable verification rule to Step 3 and Step 4 Supervisory Gates: Granular and step-level evaluations must explicitly cross-reference the deliverable in P/UI_output against every item in Step 2 stated_requirements. If any stated requirement is omitted, unaddressed, or incomplete in the proposed deliverable, evaluation must be FAIL.

agents_md_reference.requirement: Agents.md provides Failure Examples (lines 7-102) and Step3_TSR Test_Schema (lines 431-758), but provides no normative or canonical schema examples for supervisory gate inputs and outputs.

program_reference.behavior: Implementers and skills must guess the exact shape of unevaluated templates, completed PASS returns, completed FAIL returns, restart payloads, and loop control structures.

requirement_evaluations.explanation: Agents.md does not mandate that any generated informational bootstrap skill or procedural context must contain non-truncated, mechanical examples of Step 0 execution return, unevaluated supervisory gate schema, completed PASS gate, completed FAIL gate, restart-on-FAIL payload, Step 3 loop payload, and Git commit checkpoints. Without an explicit rule in Agents.md, a model omitting these examples cannot be objectively failed under Step 3.F tests.
requirement_evaluations.required_change: Add a new subsection under Bootstrap or Step 3 specifying that bootstrap procedural deliverables must include complete, non-truncated concrete JSON examples of: (1) Step 0 start_of_turn execution return, (2) Unevaluated supervisory input template with nulls, (3) Completed PASS supervisory gate return, (4) Completed FAIL supervisory gate return with recorded failure, (5) Step restart payload on FAIL, (6) Step 3 loop rejection return (Loop_Decision: True, return_to: Step_3.A), and (7) Git commit checkpoint records.

agents_md_reference.requirement: Bootstrap specifies isolated directory ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/runs/<run_nonce>/. Step 4 specifies 'Print this step's record to persistent storage.' Lines 686-687 in Test 25 mention 'Commit only; the workflow commit triggers the runtime.'

program_reference.behavior: Runner writes files locally to disk, but performs no git commits during run execution.

requirement_evaluations.explanation: Agents.md is completely silent on the requirement that a procedure of N defined steps must produce at least N durable Git commits attributable to that run. It mentions persistent storage, but does not specify Git commit boundaries, commit messages, or a checkpoint rule mandating that fewer than N commits constitutes an automatic failure.
requirement_evaluations.required_change: Add an explicit 'Git Checkpoint and Commit Protocol' to Agents.md: For any procedure with N defined steps (Steps 0 through N-1), each completed step-and-gate boundary must be durably committed to git before advancing to the next step. A completed run of N steps must possess at least N distinct git commits attributable to that run_nonce. If fewer than N commits exist, the procedure run is failed.

agents_md_reference.requirement: Bootstrap: 'Preserve the complete user utterance verbatim as the initial user message for that run.' Step 0: '"user_request":"<verbatim user request>"'. Step 1: 'The persistent record and the UI record must identify the same run_nonce, request, and request nonce.' Step 2: 'Extract only requirements stated by the user. Preserve each requirement verbatim...'

program_reference.behavior: Internal orchestration strings ('Perform exactly Step N from Agents.md...', 'This execution step is being restarted...') are prepended to prompt payloads sent to the model.

requirement_evaluations.explanation: Agents.md requires verbatim preservation of the user utterance in user_request and U, but does not explicitly warn that internal controller prompts, runner directives, or system instructions must NEVER be merged into or substituted for the user's request. When models see prompt envelopes, they occasionally confuse the controller instructions with the user request.
requirement_evaluations.required_change: Amend Bootstrap and Step 0 with an explicit negative constraint: Internal controller directives, step dispatch headers (e.g. 'Perform exactly Step N'), and supervisory repair instructions are internal control signals and must NEVER be stored, copied, or evaluated as the user_request, U, or stated_requirements. user_request and U must strictly equal the external trigger user utterance.

agents_md_reference.requirement: 'The next execution step is permitted only when gate_result is PASS. Select FAIL otherwise. Do not begin the next execution step when this value is FAIL.'

program_reference.behavior: Enforces while loop at each step, preventing progression until gate_result === 'PASS'.

requirement_evaluations.explanation: Agents.md is completely unambiguous across every step: 'The next execution step is permitted only when gate_result is PASS... Do not begin the next execution step when this value is FAIL.' An implementation that skips a failed gate or allows later steps to run directly violates this clear, repeated imperative.

transition_evaluation.explanation: The transition key supervisory_gate.gate_result with PASS/FAIL values is well-specified in Agents.md. However, the execution-to-supervisor handoff is only partial because Agents.md does not specify that the supervisor must receive the execution return inside/alongside an unpopulated template where evaluative fields begin as null.

omissions.missing_behavior: Explicit definition of the unevaluated supervisory gate schema template containing null values for all evaluative fields.
omissions.consequence: Implementers and models either invent completed schemas from scratch or pre-fill evaluations, bypassing impartial supervisory review.

omissions.missing_behavior: Explicit deliverable verification requirement tying Step 3 P/UI_output and Step 4 outputs to Step 2 stated_requirements.
omissions.consequence: Supervisors pass execution schemas that omit requested artifacts or examples as long as the JSON keys themselves exist.

omissions.missing_behavior: Git commit checkpoint protocol requiring at least N commits for N defined steps.
omissions.consequence: Runs execute entirely in ephemeral memory or uncommitted working trees without durable Git audit trails at step boundaries.

omissions.missing_behavior: Explicit examples of Step 0 returns, unevaluated templates, PASS/FAIL gate schemas, restarts, and loops.
omissions.consequence: Models cannot execute procedures mechanically and instead infer inconsistent JSON structures.

recommended_changes.change: Insert Section '## Supervisory Gate Protocol and Unevaluated Templates' into Agents.md immediately following Bootstrap. Define the unevaluated template specification where granular evaluations, comments, step-level evaluation, failures, and gate_result are initialized to null.
recommended_changes.reason: Eliminates hallucinated or pre-biased supervisory evaluations and ensures mechanical schema population.

recommended_changes.change: Insert Section '## Git Checkpoint Protocol' into Agents.md mandating that every step boundary (execution return + supervisory gate PASS) must be committed to git before advancing, requiring at least N commits for N steps.
recommended_changes.reason: Enforces durable persistence, auditability, and deterministic step boundary enforcement.

recommended_changes.change: Amend Step 3 and Step 4 Supervisory Gate instructions to mandate explicit 1:1 cross-checking of the proposed plan/deliverable against all Step 2 stated_requirements.
recommended_changes.reason: Prevents supervisors from passing deliverables that omit user-demanded specifications (such as missing return-schema examples in a generated skill).

recommended_changes.change: Add concrete JSON return-schema examples to Agents.md illustrating: (1) Step 0 start_of_turn return, (2) Unevaluated supervisory input schema, (3) Completed PASS supervisory return, (4) Completed FAIL supervisory return, (5) Restart execution payload, and (6) Step 3 loop payload.
recommended_changes.reason: Provides exact structural templates so both execution and supervisory semantic operators can operate mechanically without inference.
